source_text: Ἡμεῖς δὲ μετὰ τὸ οὕτως λοῦσαι τὸν πεπεισμένον καὶ συγκατατεθειμένον ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς ἄγομεν, ἔνθα συνηγμένοι εἰσί, κοινὰς εὐχὰς ποιησόμενοι ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτῶν καὶ τοῦ φωτισθέντος καὶ ἄλλων πανταχοῦ πάντων εὐτόνως, ὅπως καταξιωθῶμεν τὰ ἀληθῆ μαθόντες καὶ δι᾿ ἔργων ἀγαθοὶ πολιτευταὶ καὶ φύλακες τῶν ἐντεταλμένων εὑρεθῆναι, ὅπως τὴν αἰώνιον σωτηρίαν σωθῶμεν. Ἀλλήλους φιλήματι ἀσπαζόμεθα παυσάμενοι τῶν εὐχῶν. Ἔπειτα προσφέρεται τῷ προεστῶτι τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἄρτος καὶ ποτήριον ὕδατος καὶ κράματος, καὶ οὗτος λαβὼν αἶνον καὶ δόξαν τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου ἀναπέμπει καὶ εὐχαριστίαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ κατηξιῶσθαι τούτων παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πολὺ ποιεῖται· οὗ συντελέσαντος τὰς εὐχὰς καὶ τὴν εὐχαριστίαν πᾶς ὁ παρὼν λαὸς ἐπευφημεῖ λέγων· Ἀμήν. Τὸ δὲ ἀμὴν τῇ ἑβραΐδι φωνῇ τὸ γένοιτο σημαίνει. Εὐχαριστήσαντος δὲ τοῦ προεστῶτος καὶ ἐπευφημήσαντος παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ οἱ καλούμενοι παρ᾿ ἡμῖν διάκονοι διδόασιν ἑκάστῳ τῶν παρόντων μεταλαβεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐχαριστηθέντος ἄρτου καὶ οἴνου καὶ ὕδατος καὶ τοῖς οὐ παροῦσιν ἀποφέρουσι.
pass_a_gloss: We, however, after having washed thus the one who has been convinced and has assented to the things said about the brothers, lead him to where they are gathered, and we offer common prayers for themselves and for the one who has been enlightened and for all others everywhere, so that having learned the true things, we may be found to be good citizens and guardians of the things entrusted, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after stopping the prayers. Then bread and a cup of water and a mixture are offered to the one presiding over the brothers, and this one, having taken praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, sends up and makes a thanksgiving for being deemed worthy of these things by him for a long time; when he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, the whole present people shout in approval, saying: Amen. The Amen in the Hebrew language means 'so be it'. And when the presiding one has given thanks and the whole people have shouted in approval, the ones called deacons by us give to each of the present ones to partake of the bread and wine and water that have been given thanks for, and they carry away to those not present.

pass_b_english: After washing the person who has been persuaded and has assented to the things said about the brothers, we bring him to the brothers where they are gathered. There we offer common prayers for ourselves, for the one who has been enlightened, and for all others everywhere. We pray that, having learned the true things, we may be found to be good citizens and guardians of the things entrusted to us, so that we may be saved for eternal salvation. We greet one another with a kiss after we finish the prayers.

Then bread, a cup of water, and a mixture are brought to the one presiding over the brothers. He takes them and sends up praise and glory to the Father of all through the name of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. He offers a lengthy thanksgiving for being deemed worthy of these things by him. When he has finished the prayers and the thanksgiving, all the people present shout their approval, saying: Amen. In the Hebrew language, Amen means 'so be it.' After the presider has given thanks and all the people have shouted their approval, those we call deacons give each of those present a share of the bread, wine, and water over which thanks was given, and they carry portions away to those who are absent.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the liturgical sequence and the theological nuances of the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'κράματος' as 'mixture' and 'ἐπὶ τοὺς λεγομένους ἀδελφοὺς' as 'to the things said about the brothers' is faithful to the Greek syntax.
